i.norm:
Verifies that {@link X5455_ExtendedTimestamp} can serialize its timestamp data and then parse it back into an equivalent state ("parse / reparse" round trip), for both the local-file-data and the central-directory layouts.

Recall the on-disk layout of the 0x5455 ("UT") extra field:

 Flags Byte info bits: bit0 = modify time, bit1 = access time, bit2 = create time (ModTime) Long time of last modification (UTC/GMT) - present when bit0 is set (AcTime) Long time of last access (UTC/GMT) - present when bit1 is set (local data only) (CrTime) Long time of original creation (UTC/GMT) - present when bit2 is set (local data only)

The central directory only ever carries the modify time, even when the access/create bits are set.
The largest timestamp that still fits in a signed 32 bit integer of seconds.
The extra field under test.

Sets all three timestamps to {@code time}, applies {@code providedFlags}, serializes, then parses the bytes back and asserts the result.

The exercise runs twice: once over {@link X5455_ExtendedTimestamp#getLocalFileDataData()} and once over {@link X5455_ExtendedTimestamp#getCentralDirectoryData()}.

@param providedFlags the flags byte we feed in (may contain spurious high bits). @param time the timestamp value written to every enabled field. @param expectedFlags the flags byte we expect to read back (high bits dropped). @param expectedLocal the expected serialized local-file-data bytes. @param almostExpectedCentral the expected serialized central-directory bytes, except for byte 0 (the flags), which this method overwrites with {@code expectedFlags}.
The caller can't conveniently set the flags byte of the central data, so we patch it in here.

Central data never carries access or create time, but may carry modify time.
Convenience overload for the common case where the provided and expected flags are identical and equal to the flags byte of the expected local data.
Each byte[] is the expected serialized form: byte 0 is the flags byte, followed by 4-byte little-endian timestamps for each present field. -1,-1,-1,0x7f encodes Integer.MAX_VALUE.
No flags set: a single zero flags byte, no timestamps.
Central data carrying only the access (bit1) flag and no timestamp payload.
Central data carrying only the create (bit2) flag and no timestamp payload.
Single-field local layouts: flags byte + one 4-byte timestamp.
Two-field local layouts: flags byte + two 4-byte timestamps.
Three-field local layouts: flags byte + three 4-byte timestamps.
No timestamps at all.
Modify time only -> central data mirrors local data.
Access time only -> central keeps the flag but drops the payload.
Create time only -> central keeps the flag but drops the payload.
Modify + access -> central keeps only the modify time.
Modify + access + create -> central keeps only the modify time.
As far as the spec is concerned (December 2012) only the low 3 bits are meaningful, so every flags byte below is just a "spurious" variant of 7 (binary 00000111) and must normalize to 7.
